title: Worker Implementation Plan

axiomatic: Expensive simulation and coordination logic must not block the main/UI thread
Worker-backed computation must remain deterministic, versioned, and cancelable
The program must preserve responsiveness even when simulation work increases
axiological: Prioritize user interaction fluidity, modularity, and clear ownership boundaries
Prefer compact, typed, incremental communication over broad state cloning
Favor observable, testable, and maintainable concurrency over ad hoc background work
teleological: Transform workers into a first-class execution layer for the program
Scale the app toward dense, interactive scenes without UI stalls
Enable a robust foundation for future simulation, routing, geometry, and analysis workloads

objectives: Introduce a worker-backed execution model for expensive simulation tasks
Separate GUI concerns from authoritative simulation logic
Route overlap, placement, layout, and derived computation off the main thread
Support multiple workers with role-based task routing where beneficial
Preserve rendering responsiveness and interaction quality
Add cancellation, versioning, fallback, and stale-result rejection
Instrument worker health, latency, and throughput
Validate correctness and performance against current synchronous behavior
qualityGuards: Keep the main thread focused on React, rendering, input, and immediate visual feedback
Ensure every worker result is versioned and ignored if stale
Prefer deterministic reducers and pure data messages over mutable shared state
Batch or coalesce frequent intents to prevent message storms
Use transferables or compact patches for large payloads when possible
Avoid worker architectures that increase main-thread rerenders or coordination overhead
Provide graceful fallback if workers fail, are unavailable, or fall behind
Measure before and after every migration step

workstreams.name: Worker foundation
goals: Create the worker bootstrap and lifecycle management
Establish versioning, cancellation, and stale-result handling
Add fallback execution for unavailable or failing workers

phases.name: Protocol and contracts
tasks: Define command, result, patch, cancel, and error message envelopes
Add protocol version, requestId, sceneRevision, and task metadata
Create shared types for simulation intents and responses
Document worker ownership boundaries and fallback rules

phases.name: Worker runtime
tasks: Create a worker entrypoint and dispatch loop
Add lifecycle handling for init, ready, shutdown, and error states
Add cooperative cancellation and stale-result rejection
Add health and backlog tracking

phases.name: Main-thread bridge
tasks: Create a main-thread worker coordinator
Route intents from UI and store actions to workers
Apply worker patches and results in bounded batches
Keep transient UI state local and responsive

workstreams.name: Simulation offload
goals: Move expensive placement and overlap logic into workers
Reduce main-thread computation in hot interaction paths
Preserve current behavior while improving responsiveness

phases.name: Collision and placement
tasks: Move overlap checks into worker-owned logic
Move best-position search into the worker
Move bulk overlap resolution into the worker
Return resolved positions as patches or results

phases.name: Spatial indexing
tasks: Use or adapt spatial hashing inside the worker
Build worker-owned query structures for nearby candidate lookup
Avoid full-scene scans for repeated interactive placement checks

phases.name: History and derived state
tasks: Replace broad deep-clone history with patch or delta generation where applicable
Move expensive derived state computation off-thread
Keep undo and redo behavior deterministic and versioned

workstreams.name: Multi-worker architecture
goals: Support specialized workers when parallelism materially helps
Keep task routing and load balancing predictable
Avoid premature complexity while enabling future scale

phases.name: Worker roles
tasks: Define a layout worker for placement and overlap work
Define a routing worker for link and path computation
Define an analysis worker for validation and derived metrics
Optionally define an export worker for heavy offline transforms

phases.name: Pool orchestration
tasks: Implement role-based task routing
Implement least-loaded worker selection
Track active jobs, queue depth, and worker health
Keep the main thread as the coordinator

phases.name: Cancellation and stale handling
tasks: Assign task generation or revision numbers
Cancel superseded tasks when newer intents arrive
Ignore out-of-order or stale results on arrival
Track cancellation and stale-result rates in telemetry

workstreams.name: Main-thread integration
goals: Integrate workers into the existing app flow
Keep UI and simulation state distinct

phases.name: Intent dispatch
tasks: Dispatch worker intents from app-level interaction handlers
Keep pointer and camera responsiveness on the main thread
Treat the worker as the authority for expensive simulation outcomes

phases.name: Patch application
tasks: Apply worker-generated patches in bounded batches
Minimize React rerenders by collapsing redundant updates
Separate hot preview state from committed simulation state

phases.name: Rendering stability
tasks: Avoid frame-time spikes caused by worker reconciliation
Keep animation and rendering independent from worker latency
Ensure the last valid scene remains visible while new results are pending

workstreams.name: Validation and rollout
goals: Roll out worker usage safely in phases
Provide measurable evidence for every migration step

phases.name: Instrumentation
tasks: Add telemetry for task duration, queue delay, cancellation, fallback, and stale-result rejection
Record main-thread frame time and React commit pressure before migration
Track worker health and queue depth

phases.name: Shadow and canary
tasks: Run worker computations in shadow mode before using results
Compare worker output against current synchronous behavior
Enable a canary path for a subset of tasks or sessions

phases.name: Default-on migration
tasks: Route eligible simulation work to workers by default
Retain synchronous fallback for failure or unsupported environments
Remove obsolete synchronous code only after sustained stability

currentActions: Create the worker protocol types and message envelopes
Implement a worker entrypoint and main-thread bridge
Migrate overlap and placement logic first
Add versioning, cancellation, and stale-result rejection
Instrument worker telemetry and fallback paths
Validate against representative scenes and interaction traces
Add production-grade completion checks and verification checks
Expand rollout safety coverage for stale results, crash recovery, and fallback
futureActions: Expand from a single worker to a role-based worker set if profiling justifies it
Move additional derived computations into the worker layer
Use worker-assisted routing, layout, and validation for dense scenes
Add optional export and analytics workers for heavy offline tasks
Refine patch batching and render reconciliation to reduce React churn
Improve fallback behavior for unsupported browsers or degraded environments
Maintain benchmark baselines and regression checks across releases
Broaden verification coverage to include soak tests, chaos injection, and cross-version compatibility
Add automated parity checks against the synchronous baseline for representative scene corpora

strategy: Add structured logs around worker initialization, task dispatch, task completion, cancellation, and fallback
Validate payload shapes before sending and before applying results
Track scene revision numbers and discard stale results deterministically
Profile frame time and main-thread blocking before and after each migration
Compare worker-backed outputs against synchronous outputs on representative scenes
Use feature flags to isolate worker subsystems during rollout
Record queue depth, worker latency, and backpressure conditions
Expose debug overlays or diagnostics for worker state when needed
Run shadow-mode comparisons before enabling worker results in production flow
Inject delayed, duplicated, cancelled, and out-of-order messages during validation
Measure memory growth and queue saturation during long-running soak tests

completionChecks.name: Worker protocol integrity
criteria: Messages are versioned and typed
Requests and results can be correlated by requestId
Stale results are ignored safely
Cancellation works for superseded work
Invalid payloads are rejected before mutation
Protocol mismatches fail closed without corrupting state

completionChecks.name: Simulation offload success
criteria: Overlap and placement logic no longer blocks the main thread in hot paths
Results match current synchronous behavior for representative cases
Worker latency and queue depth remain within acceptable bounds
Input responsiveness remains acceptable during dense interaction
Committed scene state remains deterministic across repeated runs

completionChecks.name: Multi-worker coordination
criteria: Tasks route to the correct worker role
Load balancing favors healthy and less loaded workers
Out-of-order completion does not corrupt state
Superseded tasks are cancelled or ignored deterministically
Worker health and queue depth remain observable during load

completionChecks.name: Fallback and resilience
criteria: The app continues functioning if a worker is unavailable or fails
Fallback behavior is explicit and observable
Recovery or reinitialization does not lose committed state
Rollback to synchronous execution is possible without redeploying
Crash recovery preserves the last committed scene revision

completionChecks.name: Performance guardrails
criteria: Frame time does not regress beyond the configured threshold
React commit pressure does not regress beyond the configured threshold
Queue depth remains bounded under burst load
Main-thread input latency remains within the acceptable envelope

completionChecks.name: Parity and regression proof
criteria: Worker-backed results match the synchronous baseline on a golden corpus
Repeated runs on the same input remain deterministic
Soak tests do not reveal memory growth, drift, or result corruption

definitionOfDone: Workers are integrated into the program as a first-class execution layer
The main thread remains responsive during expensive simulation work
Simulation results are versioned, cancelable, and deterministic
Fallback paths preserve functionality when workers are unavailable
Telemetry and benchmarks demonstrate lower main-thread pressure
At least the initial collision and placement workload runs through workers successfully
The architecture is ready to expand into specialized workers when profiling justifies it
Completion checks cover protocol integrity, simulation offload, multi-worker coordination, fallback, performance guardrails, and parity
Verification checks include golden corpus comparison, crash recovery, cancellation, stale-result rejection, and soak testing
